items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: you know hear him with Jack McDuff or Grady Tate with Jimmy Smith

ctx.x: It’s interesting you say that because I used to do the same thing. I was more attuned to the saxophone players so you’d see Jerome Richardson’s on this one, and now I notice he’s on that one and all these people like playing musical chairs and said, wow, I want to do that.

Yeah. Exactly. At that early age, you know, 12, 13, I had my own bands already at school but when I saw Grady Tate, when I saw his name on an album and then saw his name on another album or I saw Joe Dukes’ name on an album and then hear him in another context, you know hear him with Jack McDuff or Grady Tate with Jimmy Smith and then

hear him on a Quincy Jones album, you know, “Smackwater Jack” and hear him play a completely different style, completely different feel, and sound as comfortable as he sounded, you know, playing a shuffle with Jimmy Smith. So, and I saw him live a bunch of times, on Broadway with Lena Horne and I heard him play in that context. I said Grady Tate is like amazing. And then I finally got to meet him and we hung out, I actually played on one of his solo records where he was the main vocalist. I was really flattered…
